note: Byte budgets for the HTML this project ships, closing the bundle half of the performance gap in docs/CONFORMANCE-GAPS.md. Bytes are exact, so these are absolute ceilings with deliberate headroom rather than ratios against a noisy measurement. Raising one is a decision: say why here, in the same commit. Measured by scripts/check_bundle_budget.py, regenerated with its --update flag; tests/test_bundle_budget.py runs the same comparison inside make test and holds the measured block, the rationale figures and the docs/BENCHMARKS.md table to a live measurement, so a stale number here fails rather than sitting quietly under its ceiling.

rationale.playgroundPageBytes: 13.5 KiB against 13.3 KiB measured. The page is a single self-contained file with no external assets bar the SRI-pinned Pyodide script, and it should stay one screenful of markup plus its boot script. This is the first time the ceiling has moved, and the argument for the 1 KiB is DISC-02 in DISCOVERY-AND-ADOPTION-STANDARD.md: the page carried no link to its own repository, so a reader who arrived from a search had no route to the CLI, the GitHub Action, the pre-commit hook, the Docker image or the editor extension, and a crawler had to infer from prose that this is software that runs in the reader's own browser. The backlink and one application/ld+json node cost 1.5 KiB between them; the reasoning about what that node deliberately leaves out lives in web/README.md rather than in a comment every visitor downloads. That left 311 bytes of headroom. The ceiling moved a second time, by 512 bytes, on 2026-09-17, for the owner's decision to count visits with Google Analytics 4 on every public site (ADR 0010): the minimum GA origins in the CSP, one sentence beside the lede saying GA never sees a feed file or the report, the analytics.js script tag and the footer opt-out control cost 573 bytes together, and the reasoning stays in ADR 0010 and web/README.md rather than in a comment every visitor downloads. That leaves 250 bytes of headroom, 1.8%, tighter again than before: this page is still not supposed to grow. The 1200x630 card itself is a static asset, not markup, and does not enter this figure.
rationale.publishedSiteBytes: 256 KiB against 246 KiB measured. The ceiling was sized when the tree was 110 KiB, so the rule catalog could roughly double before it fired; the per-page meta and canonical tags, then the share-card tags on all 47 pages, then the playground's backlink and structured data, and then the Google Analytics 4 loader, privacy page, script tag and footer opt-out on every page (ADR 0010), have since taken the tree to 246 KiB, so the remaining headroom is about fifteen more rule pages rather than a doubling. The 1200x630 card itself is a static asset, not markup, and does not enter this figure. A build that started emitting something unintended into web/ still fires it.
rationale.publishedPageCount: 60 against 49. One page per rule, two indexes and the privacy page; 46 rules today. Catches a generator that starts writing pages nobody asked for, which a byte total alone can miss.
rationale.reportBytesAt10kFindings: 3 MiB against 2.24 MiB measured, about 235 bytes per finding. This is the number that can grow silently: a template change adding 80 bytes to a row is invisible on a fixture and adds 800 KB here. FIX-15's contract is that a 10,000-finding report stays usable, and a report that has to be downloaded before it can be read is not.
